label: copy-phase input k, late in long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost only when the fed-back input token is k (99.7% of activation mass). It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, or on any other input token except a handful of x/m/r. It is rare at early steps and grows sharply with absolute step t: 41% of mass is at t=17 and 21% at t=16, so it is concentrated in L=8-9 sequences near the end of the copy. Even at t=17 only about half of k inputs activate, and no variable we tested (output token, next output, previous tokens) separated active from inactive k steps, so precision stays low. Input k in the copy phase gives recall 0.99 but precision 0.06; adding t>=14 gives mass recall 0.81 and precision 0.22.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: k, x, r, m, -, o; least: 0, f, u, p) and the token being output (most: x, h, m, 1, r, k; least: g, 0, -, b); timing cues that raise it most: t=17, recall_idx=8, L=9 & t=17.
